tion: RAN4 thanks RAN2 for the LS on In-Device Coexistence solution for EN-DC asking whether there are similar or additional IDC problems that could occur with EN-DC due to NR serving cells, and whether the current LTE IDC solution framework is suitable for those cases. RAN4 has confirmed that IDC problems not only for other systems already identified in LTE CA but also for mmWave ISM bands are expected with EN-DC. Therefore, the current LTE IDC solution framework can be reused for EN-DC cases. Note that since this kind of co-existence studies don’t impact RAN4 spec and how to solve IDC problems is left to implementation, these contents are not to be captured in RAN4 TRs with respect to each EN-DC configuration e.g. TR 37.863-01-01. 2. Actions: To RAN4: RAN4 would like to ask RAN2 to take the above information into account for the signalling design. 3. Date of Next TSG-RAN4 Meetings: TSG-RAN4 Meeting #86-bis 16th – 20th April 2018, Melbourne, Australia TSG-RAN4 Meeting #87 21st – 25th May 2018, Busan, Korea

{"chunk_id":"R2-1915870-004","collection":"ran2_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["Ericsson"],"tdocNumber":"R2-1915870","title":"Handling consistent UL LBT failures"},"point_id":"8905138501099521677"}
As observed above, the existing AM RLC mechanism for failure reporting when a bearer reaches the maximum number of RLC transmissions uses RRC signalling to report SCell RLC problems to the gNB. In section 2.3.1 we analyse how the RLC failure mechanism can be extended to cover RRC based SCell reporting of consistent UL LBT failures in SCells, and in section 3 we have the corresponding spec changes to support this. RAN2 has agreed to introduce a new MAC CE for indicating consistent uplink LBT failures in an SCell to the gNB. Whether the MAC CE can be used to report failure for primary cells (PCell or PSCell) is for further studies. In section 2.3.2 analyse how the MAC CE based solution for SCell reporting can be implemented in the spec, while section 4 has the corresponding spec changes that would be needed. Then in section 2.3.3 we compare these two alternatives.
